post: AI changes everything. Work smarter. The future is here. What do you think?

request_context.topic: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.
request_context.audience: Managers and professionals responsible for approving work, with no cybersecurity or software-development expertise assumed.
request_context.objective: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.

meaning.thesis: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.
meaning.reader_consequence: For one repeated task, compare the time to usable completion with and without AI, including checking and corrections; treat this as a proposed measurement, not a reported study result.

facts.text: The Stanford-published study of 5,172 customer-support agents reports an average15% increase in issues resolved per hour with AI assistance.
METR reports that16 experienced open-source developers completing246 tasks took19% longer with early-2025 AI tools in its randomized study.

meaning.qualification: These studies involve different workers, tasks and tools, not a matched comparison. They do not establish checking as the cause of slowdown. METR’s early-2025 result is historical; its February2026 follow-up has selection and measurement biases and does not provide a reliable current effect estimate.

beats: Begin with a familiar choice: is the work done when output appears, or when it can be used?
Compare the two attributed findings without pretending the settings are equivalent.
Explain the narrow measurement implication; distinguish proposed checking-and-correction measurement from a proven causal explanation.
End with the practical task comparison and a compact evidence boundary.

system: You are a strict LinkedIn publish-quality evaluator. Score the finished post, not the raw topic, from 0 (absent) to 5 (exceptional) on each named dimension. Judge whether the post is understandable, useful, specific, distinctive, interesting, shareable, and authentic enough to publish. Do not reward clickbait, engagement bait, unsupported specificity, or generic LinkedIn polish. Use the supplied evidence only to judge whether concrete details are grounded. This is a publish-readiness heuristic, not a promise of virality. These ratings are not calibrated to the author's human judgments or engagement outcomes. Apply the rating anchors to each dimension; never inflate scores to meet a threshold. Use the same brief and voice context as the writer. If writing_voice is present, assess voice fit against its selected style_traits over default persona style; approved examples supply compatible details only. Preserve factual and author-POV boundaries. Identify the largest fixable defect first; missing factual support is an evidence-brief gap, not permission to invent a better story. Return JSON only.
